questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The committee B. has submitted their report C. to the board D. for review.
questions.solution:
A collective noun like 'committee' takes a singular verb and singular possessive pronoun when it acts as one body. 'Has submitted' is correct, but 'their' should be 'its'. The error is in part B.

**Answer: has submitted their report**
questions.shortcut: Collective noun (committee, jury, team) acting as one unit → 'its', never 'their'.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrase:

The manager hired him purely _____, despite his lack of experience.
questions.solution:
'On merit' means on the basis of ability and qualifications — exactly what contrasts with 'despite his lack of experience'. The other phrases (on the edge, at all costs, by the book) do not fit the context of hiring.

**Answer: on merit**

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:

**Nadir**
questions.solution:
Nadir means the lowest or worst point (the opposite of zenith). Its synonym here is 'low point'; apex, zenith and peak are antonyms.

**Answer: Low point**
questions.shortcut: Nadir and zenith are a classic opposite pair — lowest and highest point.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate idiom:

His sudden resignation caught everyone _______.
questions.solution:
'Caught everyone off guard' means took everyone by surprise — the natural idiom for a sudden resignation. 'Red-handed' means caught in the act of wrongdoing; 'in limbo' and 'on thin ice' do not fit.

**Answer: off guard**

questions.q:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "bank" with the **same meaning** as in the following sentence?

"The river overflowed its bank after the storm."
options: The teller at the bank smiled as she counted the money
He used a shovel to bank the soil around the new plant
The airplane began to bank to the left as it approached the runway.
They enjoyed a picnic on the grassy bank of the stream.
questions.solution:
In the given sentence, 'bank' means the sloping ground alongside a river. The same sense appears in 'picnic on the grassy bank of the stream'; the other sentences use bank as a financial institution, as piling up soil, or as the tilting of an aircraft.

**Answer: They enjoyed a picnic on the grassy bank of the stream.**
questions.shortcut: Match the exact sense (edge of a water body), not just any use of the word.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.solution:
The correct spelling is 'Voluntary' (V-O-L-U-N-T-A-R-Y), from Latin 'voluntas' (free will).

**Answer: Voluntary**

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.solution:
The correct spelling is 'Vacuum' — double 'u' but a single 'c'.

**Answer: Vacuum**

questions.q:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:

**The icing on the cake**
questions.solution:
'The icing on the cake' refers to something extra good added to an already good thing — the best part of something, not a dessert or a minor detail.

**Answer: The best part of something**

questions.q:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:
A person who can foresee future events
questions.solution:
A 'seer' is a person who can foresee future events. Oxymoron = a self-contradictory phrase; cinephile = a film lover; pitcher = a player who throws the ball.

**Answer: Seer**

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word:

**Noxious**
questions.solution:
Noxious means harmful or poisonous, so its antonym is 'beneficial'. Toxic, poisonous and unhealthy are synonyms, not antonyms.

**Answer: Beneficial**
questions.shortcut: Nox- relates to harm (Latin 'nocere', to hurt); the answer is the positive opposite.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word:

**Pernicious**
questions.solution:
Pernicious means highly harmful or destructive, so its antonym is 'beneficial'. Harmful, detrimental and injurious are synonyms of pernicious.

**Answer: Beneficial**

questions.q:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:
A person who collects or studies butterflies
questions.solution:
Butterflies and moths belong to the order Lepidoptera, so a person who collects or studies them is a lepidopterist. An entomologist studies insects generally; an ornithologist studies birds.

**Answer: Lepidopterist**

questions.q:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

Let the documents be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.
options: You should submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
The documents will be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.
Let the head of the department submit the documents by the end of the week.
questions.solution:
A passive imperative ('Let + object + be + past participle') becomes an active imperative by starting with the base verb: 'Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.' Option A changes the meaning with 'you should', and option C remains passive.

**Answer: Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.**
questions.shortcut: 'Let ... be + V3' → drop 'let' and 'be', start with the base verb.

questions.q:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

The student said, "I have been practicing for the competition for months, but I am still nervous, as the other competitors are very skilled."
options: The student said that he has been practicing for the competition for months, but he is still nervous, as the other competitors are very skilled.
The student said that he had been practicing for the competition for months, but he was still nervous, as the other competitors were very skilled.
The student said that he had been practicing for the competition for months, but he is still nervous, as the other competitors are very skilled.
The student said that he was practicing for the competition for months, but he was still nervous, as the other competitors were very skilled.
questions.solution:
In indirect speech every verb backshifts one step: 'have been practicing' → 'had been practicing', 'am' → 'was', 'are' → 'were'. Only option B shifts all three verbs correctly.

**Answer: The student said that he had been practicing for the competition for months, but he was still nervous, as the other competitors were very skilled.**
questions.shortcut: Backshift every verb one tense; one unshifted verb is enough to reject an option.

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

In order to __**earning decent living**__ we need to have a good job with a lucrative salary.
questions.solution:
The fixed expression is 'to earn a decent living' — the article 'a' with the adjective 'decent' before 'living'. The original omits 'a'.

**Answer: earn a decent living**
questions.shortcut: 'Earn a living' is a fixed phrase — it always needs the article 'a'.

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence :

My brother works for **__a MNC.__**
questions.solution:
'MNC' is pronounced /em-en-see/, starting with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an': 'My brother works for an MNC.'

**Answer: an MNC**
questions.shortcut: Articles follow sound, not spelling: 'M' starts with a vowel sound ('em') → 'an'.

questions.q:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

People eat rice in many countries.
options: Rice was eaten by people in many countries.
Rice was eaten in many countries.
Rice is eaten in many countries.
Rice has been eaten by people in many countries.
questions.solution:
The present simple active 'People eat rice' becomes 'is/are + eaten': 'Rice is eaten in many countries.' The agent 'by people' can be dropped, and past or perfect tenses would change the meaning.

**Answer: Rice is eaten in many countries.**
questions.shortcut: Keep the original tense: present simple → is/are + past participle.

questions.q:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The CEO announced that the company had lost a significant amount of revenue last year and that they were making difficult decisions to stay afloat.
options: The CEO announced, "The company lost a significant amount of revenue last year, and we are making difficult decisions to stay afloat."
The CEO announced, "The company had lost a significant amount of revenue last year, and we were making difficult decisions to stay afloat."
The CEO announced, "The company loses a significant amount of revenue last year, and we are making difficult decisions to stay afloat."
The CEO announced, "The company lost a significant amount of revenue the previous year, and we were making difficult decisions to stay afloat."
questions.solution:
Converting back to direct speech reverses each backshift: 'had lost' → 'lost', 'were making' → 'are making', and 'last year' stays as originally spoken. Only option A does this correctly; option D keeps indirect-style 'the previous year'.

**Answer: The CEO announced, "The company lost a significant amount of revenue last year, and we are making difficult decisions to stay afloat."**
questions.shortcut: Direct ↔ indirect: reverse the backshift — past perfect → simple past, past → present.

questions.q:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. She used her little trowel to loosen the rich, black dirt.

Q. She made a shallow hole and carefully lowered a little seed into it.

R. She would now watch for the emergence of the first small sprout.

S. The ground was saturated by a soft stream of water, signifying the possibility of fresh life.
questions.solution:
The real-world planting sequence: loosen the soil with the trowel (P) → lower the seed into a shallow hole (Q) → water saturates the ground (S) → watch for the first sprout (R). So P, Q, S, R.

**Answer: P, Q, S, R**
questions.shortcut: Follow the physical sequence: prepare soil → sow → water → wait for growth.

questions.q:
**Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. He believed that the id, ego, and superego were all interrelated components of the mind.

Q. Sigmund Freud's work greatly shaped our conception of the human mind.

R. Unconscious urges often drive our conscious behavior, as per his psychoanalytic theory.

S. The conflicts which create psychological distress and worry were explained by this complex paradigm.
questions.solution:
Q introduces Freud and his influence; P states his model (id, ego, superego); R adds his theory of unconscious urges; and S, opening with 'this complex paradigm', must come last as it refers back to the model. So Q, P, R, S.

**Answer: Q, P, R, S**
questions.shortcut: Start with the name introduction (Q); 'this complex paradigm' in S must follow the model description.
